analyst.summary: Apollo Tyres delivered a strong FY26/Q4 FY26 print -- double-digit India volume growth, record truck-and-bus-radial replacement volumes, EBITDA margin expansion to 14.6%, and a materially deleveraged balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA down to 0.4x) -- but the headline profit growth (Q4 PAT +242% YoY, full-year standalone PAT +194%) is significantly flattered by a Rs 574 crore one-off tax reversal netted against a Rs 338 crore restructuring charge; normalized Q4 PAT growth is closer to +113%. The market's ~14.8x trailing P/E is calculated off that tax-boosted standalone earnings base, understating the effective multiple on recurring earnings, at a moment when natural rubber costs have jumped roughly 25% in months and management admits only half the needed price hikes have been taken -- a live near-term margin risk -- while CEAT is competing aggressively for replacement-market share. Q1 FY27 results are not yet out (no board meeting date fixed as of today; historically reported in early-mid August), so the next real read on whether pricing has caught up with rubber costs is still ahead. Hold.
